citation.authors: Yeary KHK, Johnson D, Harris N, Yu H et al
citation.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics

cited_by.title: Intermittent fasting for weight and health

record.population: Black adults with BMI of 25 or more, from five Black churches in Western New York State
record.design: Cluster randomised pilot: faith-based intermittent fasting (three churches) against continuous calorie reduction (two churches), 6 months, led by community health workers
record.finding: Weight fell in both arms (fasting -3.5 kg, calorie reduction -2.9 kg). The fasting group ate about 414 kcal a day less than the calorie-reduction group, but ate less fruit, vegetables and fibre. Satisfaction was high. The authors conclude it is feasible and larger studies are needed.
record.note: The one randomised trial in Black adults I found. A pilot built to test feasibility, with no proof that fasting beats calorie reduction.
